mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 0.5% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals an acceleration in economic output, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their prior 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and price pressures, which increases risk aversion and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month
regime_hint: dual inflation and rate hike regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by at least 1% from the previous month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by at least 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by at least 0.4pp month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and lowers earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
